candidates.title: Relational database back-end
candidates.statement: The system shall use a fully relational database back-end.
candidates.source_quote: the system must use a fully relational database back-end.

candidates.title: Work with relational structure
candidates.statement: The system shall operate within and use the relational database structure rather than working against it (no architecture that violates the relational model).
candidates.source_quote: The reporting system must work WITH the relational structure, not against it.

candidates.title: Avoid denormalization for reporting
candidates.statement: The system shall avoid denormalization approaches for reporting that require maintaining sync between a reporting store and the live database unless explicitly justified.
candidates.source_quote: "I strongly recommend against denormalization for reporting,"

candidates.title: Support analytical SQL queries
candidates.statement: The system shall support execution of complex analytical SQL queries against the relational database.
candidates.source_quote: Modern SQL databases can handle complex analytical queries if they're written properly.

candidates.title: Standards-compliant HTML output
candidates.statement: The system shall produce standards-compliant HTML output (web interface, help system, and report output) that validates against W3C standards.
candidates.source_quote: "We need to make sure all HTML output validates against W3C standards,"

candidates.title: HTML accessibility and browser compatibility
candidates.statement: The system shall ensure HTML output is compatible with different browsers and assistive technologies (e.g., screen readers).
candidates.source_quote: "This isn't just about looks - it's about compatibility with different browsers and assistive technologies."

candidates.title: Separate environments
candidates.statement: The system shall support separate development, training, and production environments.
candidates.source_quote: "We have a dev server, a training server, and production,"

candidates.title: Migrate configurations between environments
candidates.statement: The system shall provide a mechanism to migrate configurations between environments, including export/import of templates, permission settings, and saved queries.
candidates.source_quote: "What we need is a way to migrate configurations between them. Export/import of templates, permission settings, and saved queries."

candidates.title: Training environment protects production data
candidates.statement: The system shall ensure the training environment protects production data so staff can experiment without risking production data.
candidates.source_quote: "the training environment needs to be safe - staff should be able to experiment without risking production data."

candidates.title: Role-based access control
candidates.statement: The system shall implement role-based access control supporting security groups and/or roles for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups.
candidates.source_quote: "We need security groups and/or 'roles' that allow access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups."

candidates.title: Change permissions via role assignment
candidates.statement: The system shall allow a user's permissions to be changed by changing their role assignment.
candidates.source_quote: "The system should make it easy to change someone's permissions by simply changing their role assignment."

candidates.title: Predefined role access levels
candidates.statement: The system shall implement predefined roles with specified access levels: Global Admin (full system access), Local Admin (branch-level reporting/configuration), Library Manager (run approved reports, limited template modification), Staff (run reports within assigned permissions), and Patron (indirect access through OPAC displays).
candidates.source_quote:
Key points:
- Global Admin: Full system access
- Local Admin: Branch-level reporting and configuration
- Library Manager: Run approved reports, limited template modification
- Staff: Run reports within assigned permissions
- Patron: Indirect access through OPAC displays

candidates.title: Do not degrade OPAC performance
candidates.statement: The system shall be architected and operated so that reporting activity does not slow down or constrain the OPAC (public catalog).
candidates.source_quote: "If a report is running, it should not slow down the OPAC."

candidates.title: Provide data specifications (data dictionaries)
candidates.statement: The system shall provide complete data specifications (data dictionaries) for authority records, bibliographic records, order records, item records, hold/request records, and other records maintained or accessed by Management Processes, including field names, data types, and relationships.
candidates.source_quote:
The developer must provide complete data specifications for:
- Authority records
- Bibliographic records
- Order records
- Item records
- Hold/request records
- Other records maintained or accessed by Management Processes

candidates.title: Provide high-level process descriptions
candidates.statement: The system shall include thorough high-level descriptions of major processes including bibliographic record import/export, validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.
candidates.source_quote:
The developer must provide a thorough high-level description of major processes, including:
- Bibliographic record import and export
- Validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources
- Standard reports

candidates.title: Online hierarchical cross-linked help
candidates.statement: The system shall provide an online, hierarchical, cross-linked help system implemented in HTML.
candidates.source_quote: The system shall provide an online, hierarchical, and cross-linked help system in HTML.

candidates.title: Accessible help for screen readers
candidates.statement: The system shall ensure the online help system is accessible to users of screen readers.
candidates.source_quote: "The help system needs to work with screen readers."

candidates.title: High-level user error reporting
candidates.statement: The system shall provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback to users when operations or reports fail.
candidates.source_quote: The system shall provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback,

candidates.title: Low-level admin query feedback
candidates.statement: The system shall provide low-level, query-specific error feedback for administrators including specifics such as which table, which field, and the kind of error when a report or query fails.
candidates.source_quote: and shall allow low-level query-specific feedback for administrators. "When a report fails, we need to know WHY"
candidates.priority_signals: "which table, which field, what kind of error"

candidates.title: Enterprise integration assumption
candidates.statement: The system shall operate as part of an enterprise-level Library Automation System and rely on enterprise infrastructure (redundant servers, backups, network connectivity).
candidates.source_quote: AS-1: Management Processes are part of an enterprise-level Library Automation System.

candidates.title: Centralized consolidation
candidates.statement: The system shall be consolidated at a central location and accept input from and provide services to multiple locations (central single source of truth).
candidates.source_quote: AS-2: Management Processes are consolidated at a central location, and accept input and provide services to multiple locations.

candidates.title: Ensure data completeness and currency
candidates.statement: The system shall ensure that data consolidated from all locations is complete and current (data freshness and completeness across locations).
candidates.source_quote: "The challenge is making sure data from all locations is complete and current."

candidates.title: Read data from ILS modules
candidates.statement: The system shall rely on and read the data structures and functionality of the enterprise ILS, including Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, and shall not replace those modules.
candidates.source_quote: DE-1: Management Processes rely on the data structures and functionality of an enterprise-level Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging modules.

candidates.title: Vendor API and file format integration
candidates.statement: The system shall interface with vendor websites via published APIs and/or automated transfer of standard-format data files (e.g., USMARC21, EDIFACT) to ingest vendor-provided data.
candidates.source_quote: DE-2: Management Processes interface with a variety of vendor websites, via published APIs and/or automated transfer of standard-format data files (e.g., USMARC21, EDIFACT).

candidates.title: Handle optional vendor EDI data
candidates.statement: The system shall be able to handle vendor-provided EDI ordering data where present and tolerate the absence of such data at some libraries.
candidates.source_quote: "We have some vendors that provide EDI ordering data... we can't rely on it being present at every library."

candidates.title: Read-only interaction with OPAC
candidates.statement: The system shall interact with the OPAC to query patron-created holds and circulation transactions but shall not modify OPAC data.
candidates.source_quote: "The reporting system queries this data, but doesn't modify it."

candidates.title: Export formats: CSV, Excel, HTML
candidates.statement: The system shall export report output in CSV, Excel, and HTML formats.
candidates.source_quote: Excel, HTML, and CSV formats are required.

candidates.title: Support real-time reporting
candidates.statement: The system shall support real-time reporting for reports that require current data (e.g., 'what's overdue today').
candidates.source_quote: "Some reports need to be real-time - like 'what's overdue today,'"

candidates.title: Support historical reporting via warehouse
candidates.statement: The system shall support historical reporting, for example via a reporting warehouse to retain historical snapshots (e.g., 'what was the bill amount on June 30th').
candidates.source_quote: "We probably need a reporting warehouse for historical data."
candidates.priority_signals: Action item: Robert to research reporting warehouse options

candidates.title: Cancelable scheduled and running reports
candidates.statement: The system shall allow scheduled or running reports to be cancelled and shall check for cancellation signals during report processing.
candidates.source_quote: The ability to cancel a scheduled or running report is technically feasible, but requires the system to check for cancellation signals during report processing.

candidates.title: Include nulls and blanks in results
candidates.statement: The system shall include null and blank fields in query and report results (explicitly include nulls rather than omitting them).
candidates.source_quote: "All nulls and blank fields must be included in the results,"

candidates.title: Filter by survey name
candidates.statement: The system shall allow filtering by survey name (not just survey ID) by resolving survey names to IDs internally.
candidates.source_quote: The ability to filter by survey name rather than survey ID requires the system to resolve names to IDs internally.
